intro: Caracas rewards visitors with vibrant neighbourhoods, mountain views and a lively food scene, though safety needs care. Pick how long you have and what you enjoy most.
tour_note: Check the tour page for which entry tickets are included.

notes: Metro is clean, cheap and fast; buy a single, round trip or 10-journey multi abono.
Metrobuses link metro stations to areas off the underground, but run roughly every 20 minutes.
Por puesto minibuses are cheap but slow, crowded and often in poor condition.
Taxis have no meters; agree the price first and expect quotes near double the fair fare.
Ride apps like Uber and inDrive work in Caracas but coverage varies; confirm before relying on them.
Driving is hectic; walking is fine by day in safe districts, but avoid quiet streets after dark.

pantheon.name: National Pantheon of Venezuela
pantheon.hours: Tue–Sun roughly 09:00–16:00 · closed Monday · check on the day
pantheon.tip: Bolivar's tomb sits under the central dome; dress modestly and keep quiet, it is a working memorial.

bolivar_birthplace.name: Birthplace of Simon Bolivar
bolivar_birthplace.price_text: Small entry fee; confirm price at the door
bolivar_birthplace.hours: Tue–Sun daytime · closed Monday · check on the day
bolivar_birthplace.tip: The colonial courtyard and period furniture are the highlight; allow less than an hour.

university_city.name: University City of Caracas
university_city.hours: Campus grounds open daytime on weekdays
university_city.tip: A UNESCO-listed modernist campus; the covered plaza and murals are the star, but stay on main paths.

los_proceres.name: Los Proceres
los_proceres.tip: A long open boulevard of statues and fountains; go in daylight and keep valuables out of sight.

diverxity.name: Diverxity
diverxity.price_text: Paid entry; check current price and hours
diverxity.tip: A family entertainment venue; confirm opening times before you travel across town.

pabellon_criollo.name: Pabellón Criollo
pabellon_criollo.price_text: Plate price varies by restaurant; budget a mid-range meal
pabellon_criollo.hours: Lunch and dinner at most criollo restaurants
pabellon_criollo.tip: Venezuela's national plate: shredded beef, black beans, rice and fried plantain. Try it at a sit-down criollo restaurant.

mercado_municipal.name: Mercado Municipal de Chacao
mercado_municipal.price_text: Free to enter; pay per stall
mercado_municipal.hours: Daily roughly 06:00–17:00 · check on the day
mercado_municipal.tip: Go early for fruit, arepas and fresh juice; bring small notes and keep your phone pocketed.

altamira_square.name: Plaza Francia and Altamira walk
altamira_square.hours: Open daily · daytime and early evening
altamira_square.tip: A leafy square for people-watching and a coffee; the surrounding streets are good for an easy stroll.

avila_viewpoint.name: El Ávila (Waraira Repano) cable car viewpoint
avila_viewpoint.price_text: Cable car ticket; check price and operating days
avila_viewpoint.hours: Check on the day · often closed some weekdays
avila_viewpoint.tip: Ride up for cool air and city views; confirm the cable car is running before you set out.

sabana_grande_walk.name: Sabana Grande boulevard walk
sabana_grande_walk.tip: A busy pedestrian shopping street; go in daylight with a local and keep bags close.

las_mercedes_dining.name: Las Mercedes restaurant strip
las_mercedes_dining.price_text: Mid-range to upscale; pay per restaurant
las_mercedes_dining.hours: Mostly lunch and dinner, later on weekends
las_mercedes_dining.tip: The city's main dining and nightlife cluster; book ahead on weekends and arrange a taxi home.

museo_bellas_artes.name: Museo de Bellas Artes
museo_bellas_artes.price_text: Low entry fee; check on the day
museo_bellas_artes.hours: Tue–Sun daytime · closed Monday · check on the day
museo_bellas_artes.tip: Venezuelan and international art in a park setting; pair it with a walk in the surrounding gardens.

parque_del_este.name: Parque del Este (Generalísimo Francisco de Miranda)
parque_del_este.price_text: Small entry fee; check on the day
parque_del_este.tip: Big green park with paths and small lakes; go in daylight and stick to busy areas.

arepa_breakfast.name: Arepa breakfast stop
arepa_breakfast.price_text: Cheap local meal; pay per item
arepa_breakfast.tip: Order a grilled arepa with cheese or shredded beef and a coffee; simple, filling and cheap.

city_tour.name: Guided city tour of central Caracas
city_tour.price_text: Price varies by operator; agree the rate first
city_tour.tip: A local guide is the easiest way to see the historic centre safely; confirm what is included before paying.

plaza_bolivar.name: Plaza Bolívar and historic centre walk
plaza_bolivar.tip: The colonial square is the heart of old Caracas; visit in daylight with a guide and skip it after dark.

cafe_altamira.name: Altamira café stop
cafe_altamira.price_text: Pay per item; café prices vary
cafe_altamira.tip: Caracas runs on coffee; a café stop is a cheap way to rest between sights and watch the city.

parque_naciones_unidas.name: Parque Naciones Unidas
parque_naciones_unidas.tip: A large open park good for a shaded walk; go in daylight and keep to the main paths.

cable_car_base.name: Waraira Repano cable car base station
cable_car_base.price_text: Ticket price varies; check on the day
cable_car_base.hours: Check operating days before you go
cable_car_base.tip: Arrive early to avoid queues and bring a light jacket, it is much cooler at the top.

heladeria.name: Heladería stop for local ice cream
heladeria.tip: Try tropical fruit flavours like parchita and mango; a cheap way to cool down.

stays.why: Central, walkable and close to the metro; good base for museums and plazas. Check the exact rate on the day.
Best for food and nightlife; many restaurants and bars within walking distance.
Cheapest of the four and near the main museums and parks; busier and less polished at night.
Quiet, leafy streets with cafés and offices; a calm base between Altamira and Las Mercedes.

food: Try an arepa: grilled corn bread filled with cheese, shredded beef or black beans. Cheap and everywhere.
Pabellón criollo is the national plate: shredded beef, rice, black beans and fried plantain.
Las Mercedes has the widest choice of restaurants and cafés; book ahead on weekends.
Street grills and bakeries are the cheapest meals. Prices in VES move fast, so ask before you order.
Coffee is strong and local. Order a cortadito at a café counter for a quick, cheap stop.
more_time: Ride the cable car up El Ávila (Waraira Repano) for city views and cool air; check it is running on the day.
Add a day for the colonial centre and the birthplace of Simón Bolívar, if it is open to visitors.
Food lovers can swap one museum morning for a market visit and a long lunch in Las Mercedes.
